answer: Randomized Inlet Quota Assignment. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon seeds a permutation that assigns new identities to one of many narrow registration inlets, each with a fixed admission quota. An attacker cannot precompute which inlet will be contested, so mass pre-registration collapses into oversubscribed slots and most sybils are rejected. Rejected attempts must pay the full verification cost per identity, while honest users face the same fee only once, mirrored by a refund on success. The umber audit log records every attempt, making repeated failures visible and costly.
